notes: First-12-month job ratings for New York City's four previous mayors, for overlay on the Mamdani tracker. months_since_inauguration = (field-period midpoint - Jan 1 inauguration) in days / 30.4375, to one decimal. metric='approve_disapprove' means a direct approve/disapprove question (Quinnipiac, Siena 2014, Marist 2022). metric='excellent_good' means Marist's or Siena's excellent/good/fair/poor scale: 'approve' holds excellent+good and 'disapprove' holds fair+poor. Those are NOT the same measure and should be a separate series or left off the approve line. Population: RV = registered voters, adults = all New York City adults/residents. Every number was read from the URL given: a pollster release, tables or trend PDF, except where confidence notes say otherwise. Known gaps: CBS News/New York Times NYC polls of June 4-8 2002, August 2002 and June 1994 exist (ICPSR studies 3697, 3703 and 6598) but their toplines could not be fetched (ICPSR returns 403), so none are recorded. Quinnipiac's online archive has no 1994 New York City polls, so Giuliani's first year rests on a single Marist reading. Updated 2026-10-02 in the admiring-jennings session: added CBS News/New York Times Bloomberg polls (June and August 2002) from CBS's own pages, New York Times/WCBS-TV Giuliani polls (June and September-October 1994) from Internet Archive copies of the Times' own articles, and field dates for the Marist March 2002 reading from Marist's archived release. Every addition was fetched and quoted by this session, not only by a research agent.
